original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as segment visibility graphs of finite collections of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Open Problem 13: "Characterize the segment visibility graphs."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the characterization problem, not the recognition or reconstruction problems, and it correctly keeps the scope to finite sets of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.
missing_details: In this paper, a segment visibility graph is the graph on the endpoints of the segments, not a graph whose vertices are the segments themselves.
If S = {s_1, ..., s_n} with endpoints p_i, q_i, then the graph has vertex set {p_1, q_1, ..., p_n, q_n}; equivalently, any realization uses exactly two graph vertices per segment.
The two endpoints of every original segment s_i are always adjacent in the graph by definition.

For endpoints x and y belonging to different segments, adjacency means that the straight segment joining x and y is unobstructed by the segment set under the paper's convention; in particular, it may not pass through another endpoint or graze/overlap a segment.
To be stand-alone, the question should specify that the goal is a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the finite graphs realizable in this sense, up to graph isomorphism.
The paper treats these as ordinary finite undirected graphs.

If you want the geometric restriction fully explicit, 'pairwise disjoint' should be understood as the segments themselves being mutually disjoint in the plane, so they do not cross or share endpoints.
refined_question: Characterize precisely the finite undirected graphs G that occur as segment visibility graphs (segment endpoint visibility graphs) of finite sets S = {s_1, ..., s_n} of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane: if s_i has endpoints p_i and q_i, then V(G) = {p_1, q_1, ..., p_n, q_n}, each pair p_iq_i is an edge of G, and for endpoints x and y lying on different segments, xy is an edge of G exactly when the straight segment joining x and y is otherwise disjoint from every segment of S, under the paper's convention that it may neither pass through another endpoint nor graze along a segment.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's full segment-visibility characterization problem, whose nearest official formulation is Open Problem 13 in Section 3.1. The surrounding Section 3.1 text explicitly distinguishes recognition, characterization, and reconstruction for segment visibility graphs, so the refined version should stay with characterization alone. To make the question self-contained and faithful to the paper, one must import the Section 1 definition: the graph's vertices are segment endpoints; visibility is defined between endpoints with the paper's strict obstruction convention; and the two endpoints of each original segment are additionally joined by an edge. The paragraph immediately before Open Problem 13 also notes that only a K5-minor-free subclass is currently characterized, confirming that the intended target is the full class, not that special subclass.
